details.summary: A highly practical, no-cook lunch that perfectly balances the flavor profile of a classic Waldorf salad while effortlessly hitting all the required nutritional targets for liver and blood sugar management.

dimensions.feedback: The flavor profile is a classic, well-balanced Waldorf: creamy yogurt, sharp Dijon and lemon, sweet grapes, and savory walnuts, offset nicely by the peppery bite of the arugula base.
All listed ingredients are used correctly in the instructions, and no surprise ingredients appear.
The no-cook instructions are clear, properly sequenced, and cover everything a beginner needs to prep and assemble the dish.
Perfectly aligns with a Modern American cafe-style lunch.
The no-cook assembly method is perfectly suited for canned chicken and fresh ingredients.
The nutrition panel aligns well with the ingredients; 43g of protein makes sense for 7oz of chicken and Greek yogurt, and the carbohydrates properly reflect the whole-grain bread and grapes.

The title is accurate and the intro sets realistic, appetizing expectations without making banned health claims. Calling out the fresh grapes vs. dried fruit highlights the diabetes-friendly swap gracefully.
A highly appetizing, quick, and crunchy lunch option that feels like a treat while staying strictly on plan.
Excellent dual-purpose design. It replaces saturated fat (mayo) with a lean protein source (yogurt) for the liver, and utilizes whole-grain complex carbs and intact fruit for steady blood sugar.

Spot on. Zero added sugar (sweetness relies entirely on whole fresh grapes) and it successfully provides a robust, quality carbohydrate base (50.5g) to fuel the reader through the afternoon without risking hypoglycemia.
Fits the Lunches chapter perfectly. It's a classic open-faced sandwich that travels well if the components are kept separate until lunchtime.
Easily achievable in the stated 10 minutes from cold start to plate. Uses readily available supermarket staples (canned chicken, standard produce, regular yogurt).
